question: For the one J9F complete first public record, how much can the 8,137 uncomputed private-error second laws alter the full conditional second public law and any fixed-target 0-1 Bayes decision under each unchanged fixed public action?
fork_classification: J9F supplies the exact first-record denominator, while J8I supplies 55 stored complete second laws. The two fixed action branches and three independent reversible diagnostics—full-law equality replay, worst-case mixture total variation, and bounded-target decision/information limits—share the same inputs and fit a zero-Born five-CPU-second matrix; no human choice of which to run first is needed.

hypotheses.small_worst_case: All 55 known complete laws coincide separately under both fixed actions. Their exact posterior weight leaves an omitted mixture fraction below one percent, yielding an action-specific total-variation and fixed-target 0-1 Bayes-gain cap equal to that fraction.
hypotheses.known_law_heterogeneity: At least one known complete public law differs under a fixed action; reject the single-Q contamination reduction and report the mismatch without inferring a small bound.
hypotheses.integrity_failure: J9F denominator, known masks/masses, prior, action binding, full public-array law normalization or source hash fails; withhold all bounds.

model_boundary: R6AF ideal periodic L=2 D4 projector/fusion instrument with exact 36-edge IID red-X p_X=1/10, p_Z=0 and the one J8I/J9F complete first public flux/charge/vacuum record. Treat [0] and [1,30,32,34,35] as separate fixed relation-free public charge actions. Private error and target labels are analysis-only, never action inputs. An optional 0-1 Bayes bound concerns a fixed hidden target and observation-independent loss, not adaptive JIT action selection or unconditional Boolean-union schedule scoring.

matrix.cells: Replay all 55 exact full flux/charge/vacuum second laws under each of the two fixed actions (110 stored laws), plus all 8,192 J9F prior-weighted first masses and known-mask membership.
matrix.exact_bound: If every known law under action a equals Q_a and epsilon is the exact posterior weight of omitted errors at the selected first record, any full law is M_a=(1-epsilon)Q_a+epsilon R_a for an unknown valid R_a. Therefore TV(M_a,Q_a)<=epsilon; probability of any event changes by at most epsilon. For a fixed hidden target with 0-1 loss, the maximum benefit from observing the second public record is at most epsilon. Also I(E;O2|O1=o1,a)<=h2(epsilon)+epsilon log2(8137) bits; the numeric bit bound is conservative and not a measured information gain.
matrix.independent_unit: One exact prior/error mass or stored action-bound complete public law; no stochastic sampling uncertainty.
matrix.integrity: Pin J9F result and contract and J8I result, replay all prior masses, 55 exact known memberships, 110 normalized full public laws, both action IDs, first/second flux consistency and exact known-law equality. Preserve unknown-law status: never impute an omitted law or per-outcome posterior guarantee.

acceptance: Recompute J9F's selected-record denominator and 55-known-law posterior weight from all 8,192 exact first masses
Replay all 110 stored complete public laws under the two fixed actions and require equality within each action before reducing to one Q

Report exact worst-case TV and fixed-target 0-1 Bayes-gain caps plus conservative private-error information cap with explicit one-record/fixed-action boundaries; no actual second-law mixture or full-IID claim
stop_rule: Stop after the two fixed-action certificates or first five-CPU-second/source/normalization/action/replay failure. Do not compute omitted complete laws, relax the public action, bootstrap, sample histories, fit risk, or widen compute/scope.
